title: Collective Organization of String Fragmentation
authors: Romuald A. Janik, Maciej A. Nowak, Marek M. Rams, Ismail Zahed
abstract: How coherent confining strings reorganize into hadronic matter is a central open problem in nonequilibrium gauge dynamics. Using real-time tensor-network simulations of the massive Schwinger model, we identify a collective organization underlying string fragmentation. For intermediate masses, the dynamics simplifies and more than $99\%$ of the temporal evolution of the electric-field probability distribution is governed by a single collective mode whose decay tracks the survival probability of the parent string. The extracted survival law exhibits the same Gaussian dependence implied by the Lund world-sheet area law, providing microscopic support for its characteristic area law dependence without assuming the Lund fragmentation mechanism. The same mode controls the transition from the coherent string to the produced mesons, explains the universal non-thermal effective fluid equation of state, and essentially controls the growth of bipartite entanglement through the causal propagation of massive pairs. These results identify collective fragmentation as an organizing principle of coherent string breaking and provide a microscopic perspective on the dynamical origin of a central ingredient of Lund hadronization.
summary: This work uses real-time tensor-network simulations on the massive Schwinger model to study string fragmentation, a key process in high-energy physics. The research identifies that the entire complex process is governed by a single collective mode in the electric-field probability distribution. This finding provides microscopic support for the characteristic Gaussian decay law associated with Lund hadronization, linking quantum dynamics to established phenomenological models.
main_problem: The paper addresses the fundamental open problem of understanding the dynamical mechanism by which coherent confining strings reorganize into hadronic matter (hadronization).
main_result: The string fragmentation process is shown to be governed by a single collective mode in the electric-field probability distribution, which yields a Gaussian survival law matching the functional form of the Lund area law.
method: The study employs real-time tensor-network simulations (Matrix-Product-State formulation) applied to the massive Schwinger model to track the evolution of the electric-field probability distribution.
model_or_system: The physical system is the massive Schwinger model (QED in 1+1 dimensions), which is used to model confinement, Schwinger pair production, and subsequent meson formation. The dynamics are simulated using a lattice Hamiltonian and analyzed via tensor networks.
key_observables: String survival probability $S(t)$, electric-field probability distribution $p_E(t)$, bipartite entanglement entropy $	ext{SEE}(t)$, and the effective equation of state for the produced mesonic 'dust'.
important_parameters: Fermion mass $m$, coupling constant $g$, and the ratio $m/g$. The analysis is valid in the intermediate mass regime.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the dynamics can be effectively described by a single collective mode, and the results provide functional support for the Lund law without deriving the full mechanism.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the space-time picture of fragmentation, the decay of the string survival factor $S(t)$ against a Gaussian fit, and the decomposition of the probability distribution dynamics into a single dominant principal component.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the problem using the massive Schwinger model, applies real-time tensor-network simulations to analyze the electric-field probability distribution, identifies the single collective mode governing the decay, and uses this mode to explain the universal equation of state and entanglement growth.
why_interesting: The use of tensor networks to model non-equilibrium dynamics in a confining gauge theory provides a concrete, computational framework for understanding complex many-body processes like hadronization, linking quantum information measures (entanglement) to physical observables.
analysis_basis: full PDF text, analyzed in chunks

figures.caption: FIG. 1. Space-time picture of string fragmentation in the massive Schwinger model. At gt ≪1, receding external charges on x = ±t are joined by a coherent electric string; at gt ≫1, the string has fragmented into an approximately boost-invariant, weakly interacting mesonic dust.

FIG. 2. In (a), we show normalized coherent-string survival factor, S(t), from the midpoint electric field. Tensor-network data are compared with the Gaussian Lund-area-law fit, Eq. (2). In (b), mass dependence of the string breaking coefficient is compared to Schwinger effect estimate with and without screening. In (c), we show dominant principal-component amplitude, Eq. (9), of (multidimensional-) midpoint electric field probability distributions. The independent Gaussian fit reproduces the string survival probability.

FIG. 3. In (a), we show the fraction of temporal variance of electric field probabilities explained by the leading PCA component. In (b), we show full tensor-network probability distribution (solid) and leading-principal-component reconstruction (dashed) for m/g = 0.5. Their near agreement shows that one collective mode captures the observable probability redistribution. In (c), analogous plot for m/g = 0 clearly requires higher dimensional evolution.

FIG. 4. Midpoint electric-field probability distributions at m/g = 0.5 for, in (a), the coherent parent-string state [62] and, in (b), the fragmented mesonic (“dust”) state. Fragmentation transfers probability from the string sector to screened configurations along a single dominant direction in probability space. In (c), we show effective equation of state in the coarse-grained fragmentation model. The survival probability controls the transfer of energy from the confining string, p ≃−ϵ, to an expanding mesonic medium with a small positive longitudinal pressure.

FIG. 5. In (a), entanglement entropy (averaged over two neighboring sites at x = 0) of the individual electric field components of the wave function with the mesonic dust probability for comparison (m/g = 0.5). In (b), bipartite entropy SEE(t) at in the middle of the chain (solid), and the causal prediction of Eq. (16) (dashed), fitting only S∞. In (c), we show linear dependence between S∞and (m/g)2.
